p.docTitle:
Federal Chancellery Ordinance
on Electronic Voting

preamble.p:
based on Articles 27e paragraph 1bis, 27g paragraph 2, 27i paragraph 3 and 27l paragraphs 3 and 4 of the Ordinance of 24 May 1978
SR 161.11 on Political Rights (PoRO),

content.p: This Ordinance regulates the requirements for authorising electronic voting trials.

blockList.listIntroduction: In this Ordinance:

item.p: system is the generic term for all the software and infrastructures that are used to conduct electronic ballots;
online system means the part of the system that is used to verify eligibility to vote, to cast the encrypted vote and to store the encrypted vote;

the trustworthy part of the system is the part of the system that includes one or more groups of control components; the trustworthiness of this part of the system arises from the fact that misuse can be detected even if only one of a group’s control components is functioning correctly;
control components are separate components of the system that are designed in a variety of ways, operated by different persons and secured by special means;
system operator means the authority or private company that operates and maintains the online system at a ballot as directed by the canton;

operation means any action, including maintenance, with a technical, administrative or legal aspect and related management activities, carried out by a canton, system operator or printing office that are required to conduct electronic ballots;
operating body means an organisation or organisational unit responsible for operation, such as a cantonal chancellery, a system operator or printing office;
auditor means a person who checks on behalf of the canton that the ballot is correctly conducted;

infrastructure means hardware, software of third-party components in accordance with Article 11 paragraph 2 letter a, network elements, premises, services and equipment of any nature at any operating bodies that are required for the secure operation of electronic voting;
software means the entire implementation originating from the cryptographic protocol for complete verifiability that is carried out by the system developer for electronic voting;

cryptographic protocol means a protocol with cryptographic security functions to meet the requirements in Number 2 of the Annex; the cryptographic protocol is located in the model level and therefore does not contain direct instructions for implementation, but instead abstract security functions;
user device means any multifunctional, programmable device that is connected to the internet and is used to vote, such as a conventional computer, a smartphone or a tablet;
registered vote means a vote the final casting of which has been acknowledged by the trustworthy part of the system;
in the case of popular votes: vote for a proposal, a counter-proposal or a deciding question,
in the case of elections: the choice of a list or of a candidate;

blockList.listIntroduction: vote cast in conformity with the system is a vote:

item.p: that complies with a predetermined way of completing a ballot paper in a vote or election,
that a sender has confirmed as final,

in respect of which the client-side authentication credentials used or the resulting authentication messages match the server authentication credentials established in the preparatory phase of the ballot and assigned to an voter, and
that has been cast using authentication credentials that have not already been used to cast a vote that has already been registered by the trustworthy part of the online system;

client-side authentication credential means a piece of information, such as a PIN, given to an individual voter that he or she requires, in some cases with other client-side authentication credentials, to be able to vote;

server-side authentication credential means a piece of information that is required, in some cases with other server-side authentication credentials, to authenticate the sender of a vote as a voter based on authentication messages;

authentication message means any information that a user device sends to the online system on submission of the client-side authentication credential so that the online system authenticates the sender of a vote as the voter;
a certificate is a document that confirms that an examined item conforms to a certain reference framework or standard;

an electronic certificate is a data record that confirms certain characteristics of a person or object and whose authenticity and integrity can be verified by cryptographic procedures; the electronic certificate is mainly used to identify and authenticate the holder, but also to encrypt messages;
critical actions and operations are processes in which critical data are processed;
critical data are data whose integrity or confidentiality is decisive in meeting the cryptographic protocol requirements.

content.p: Further definitions are provided in Number 1 of the Annex.

article.heading: Basic requirements for the authorisation of electronic voting for the individual ballots

blockList.listIntroduction: Authorisation is required for each individual ballot; it is granted if the following requirements are met:

item.p: The system is designed and operated so as to guarantee verifiable, secure and trustworthy electronic voting.
The system is easy to use for the voters; account must be taken of the special needs of all voters wherever possible.
The system and the operational procedures are designed and documented so that the details of the technical and organisational procedures can be checked and understood.
The public have access to information appropriate to the addressees on how the system works and its operational processes, and there are incentives for experts among the public to participate.

content.p: The canton shall conduct a risk assessment in which it demonstrates and justifies that the security risks in its area of responsibility are sufficiently low. The level of public trust in and acceptance of electronic voting must also form part of the assessment.

It shall check whether it can itself assess risks within the field of activity of its service providers and to what extent separate risk assessments by these service providers are required. If necessary, it shall request these separate risk assessments.

blockList.listIntroduction: The risk assessments cover the following security objectives:

item.p: the accuracy of the result;
preserving voting secrecy and excluding premature partial results;
availability and operability of the voting system;
protecting personal information relating to voters;
protecting information intended for voters from manipulation;
ensuring that evidence of voting behaviour is not maliciously exploited.

blockList.listIntroduction: Each risk must be identified and clearly described on the basis of the documentation on the system and its operation with regard to the following criteria:

item.p: security objectives;
any data records related to the security objectives;
threats;
weaknesses.

content.p: It must be possible to detect any manipulation that leads to a falsification of the result while preserving voting secrecy (complete verifiability). This is considered to be the case if requirements for individual and universal verifiability are met.

blockList.listIntroduction: The requirements for individual verifiability are as follows:

item.p: The person voting is given the opportunity to ascertain whether the vote as entered on the user device has been manipulated or intercepted on the user device or during transmission; to this end, the person voting receives proof that the trustworthy part of the system (Art. 8) has registered the vote as it was entered by the person voting on the user device as being in conformity with the system; proof of correct registration is provided for each partial vote.

A voter who has not cast his or her vote electronically can request proof after the electronic voting system is closed and within the statutory appeal deadlines that the trustworthy part of the system has not registered any vote cast using the client-side authentication credential of the voter.

blockList.listIntroduction: The requirements for universal verifiability are as follows:
The auditors receive proof that the result has been established correctly; the proof confirms that the result ascertained includes the following votes:

item.p: all votes cast in conformity with the system that have been registered by the trustworthy part of the system;
only votes cast in conformity with the system;
all partial votes in accordance with the proof generated in the individual verification process.
The auditors evaluate the proof in an observable procedure; to do so, they must use technical aids that are independent of and isolated from the rest of the system.

blockList.listIntroduction: The soundness of the proofs under Article 5 is based on the trustworthiness:

item.p: of the trustworthy part of the system for proofs under Article 5 paragraphs 2 and 3;
of the procedure for generating and printing the voting papers for proofs under Article 5 paragraph 2; and
of the technical aids used by the auditors for the audit for proofs under Article 5 paragraph 3.

article.heading: Preservation of voting secrecy and exclusion of premature partial results

blockList.listIntroduction: The trustworthiness of:

item.p: the trustworthy part of the system;
the procedure for generating and printing the voting papers;

content.p: is decisive in preserving voting secrecy and excluding premature partial results within the infrastructure.

article.heading: Requirements for the trustworthy part of the system

content.p: The trustworthy part of the system includes one or more groups of control components.
Even if only one of the control components in each group functions correctly, the proof is still sound (Art. 6) and voting secrecy is still preserved (Art. 7).
The trustworthiness of the trustworthy part of the system is guaranteed by the diverse design of the control components and the independence of their operation and supervision.

If the risks are not sufficiently low despite the measures taken, additional measures must be taken to minimise risks. This applies in particular even if all the requirements of the Annex have already been met.

blockList.listIntroduction: Independent entities commissioned by the Federal Chancellery shall examine:

item.p: the cryptographic protocol (Annex No 26.1);
the system software (Annex No 26.2);
the security of infrastructure and operation (Annex No 26.3);
the protection against attempts to infiltrate the infrastructure (Annex No 26.4).

content.p: The canton shall ensure that the system operator has an information security management system (ISMS) and this is examined by independent entities (Annex No 26.5). The ISMS shall as a minimum comprise the system operator’s processes and infrastructure that are relevant to achieving the security objectives.

The canton shall ensure that the Federal Chancellery and the independent entities that it commissions to conduct the examinations under paragraph 1 are given access to the system and the required documents.

The authorities responsible for the examinations under paragraphs 1 and 2 shall publish the evidential documents and certificates. Further documents must also be published if they are relevant for comprehensibility. Documents or parts of documents do not need to be published if there is a justified exemption, in particular under the law on freedom of information or data protection.

article.heading: Disclosure of the source code and of the documentation on the system and its operation

blockList.listIntroduction: The canton shall ensure that the following documents are published:

item.p: the source code of the system software including files with relevant parameters;
evidence that the machine-readable programmes were generated from the published software source code;
the software documentation;
the development process documentation;
instructions and other documents that experts require to be able to compile, execute and analyse the system on the basis of the source code within their own infrastructure;
technical specifications of the main components of the system;
the process documentation for operating, maintaining and securing the system;
information on and descriptions of known flaws.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following need not be published:

item.p: the source code for third-party components such as operating systems, databases, web and application servers, rights management systems, firewalls or routers, provided they are widely used and regularly updated;
the source code for portals of authorities that are connected to the system;
documents or parts of documents for which an exemption from publication is justified, in particular under the law on freedom of information or data protection.

content.p: The documents to be published under Article 11 must be drawn up and documented in such a way that they are easy to read and analyse.

blockList.listIntroduction: In order to facilitate their examination by the public, the documents must be:

item.p: available online in a simple process that is free of charge and does not require registration; and
made available in good time before the planned use of the system.

content.p: Any person may examine, modify, compile and execute the source code for ideational purposes and write reports thereon. They may publish reports and findings relating to flaws. They may have discussions with others, in particular in order to identify flaws, and in doing so may quote from the published information.

blockList.listIntroduction: The proprietor of the source code may:

item.p: permit the source code to be used for other purposes;

set specific conditions for submitting suggestions for improving the system; it may call for flaws to be reported without delay and specify a date before which reports on suspected flaws may not be published.

content.p: If the proprietor of the source code issues conditions of use for the source code and the documentation, or conditions under paragraph 4 letter b, it may only take civil or criminal legal action in the event of any breach thereof if a person has made commercial or productive use of the source code or parts thereof. The conditions of use and conditions under paragraph 4 letter b shall make reference to this.

blockList.listIntroduction: The canton shall designate a body to which interested persons may submit suggestions for improving the system, including:

item.p: suggestions relating to flaws in the documents published under Article 11;
suggestions on the basis of attempts to intrusion in the online system as part of public tests.

content.p: The body under paragraph 1 shall evaluate the suggestions and inform the person concerned of its assessment and of any measures taken based on the suggestion. This information shall be published.
The canton shall ensure that suitable financial reward is given for suggestions that relate to security and that help to improve the system.

article.heading: Responsibility for running the ballot with electronic voting correctly

content.p: The canton bears overall responsibility for running the ballot with electronic voting correctly.
It must carry out important tasks itself. It may delegate the development of the software used, operational tasks and communication on questions about how the system works to external organisations.

blockList.listIntroduction: The canton shall appoint a body at cantonal level that bears overall responsibility, and for the following tasks in particular:

item.p: drawing up general information security policy;
drawing up information classification and processing policy for the information resources identified;
drawing up risk management policy;
defining and implementing measures to ensure compliance with the policies in letters a–c;
appointing a system operator and drawing up the requirements for its supervision and monitoring;
setting the deadlines for carrying out critical actions and operations;
supervising and monitoring the system operator’s work;
supporting and instructing the auditors;
assessing and communicating the accuracy of the result of the ballot based on the proofs under Article 5 and other indicators.

content.p: When a ballot is held, the operating bodies bear responsibility towards the canton for the preparation and handling of the technical aspects of electronic voting.
The auditors under cantonal law are responsible for operating their own technical aids.

blockList.listIntroduction: Applications submitted under Article 27e PoRO must be accompanied by information on the planned use of the electronic voting channel and documents on how the legal requirements are met. These include the following in particular:

item.p: up-to-date risk assessments under Article 4, including the information necessary to make them comprehensible;
certificates and their attachments produced in examinations under Article 10 paragraph 2 and information on their publication in accordance with Article 10 paragraph 4;
information on the disclosure of the documents under Article 11 and suggestions from the public under Article 13;
reports on tests that the canton has carried out, and indications of existing flaws in the system;
justification and any measures regarding exemptions under Article 16 paragraph 2.

content.p: Reference may be made to documents under paragraph 1 that the Federal Chancellery has already received and which are still valid.
The detailed technical and administrative requirements for electronic voting are regulated in the Annex.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Chancellery may in exceptional cases exempt a canton from meeting individual requirements, provided:

item.p: the requirements that have not been met are indicated in the application;
reasonable justification is brought forward for allowing an exemption; and
the canton describes any alternative measures and justifies in reference to the risk assessment why it regards the risks as sufficiently low.

content.p:
The FCh Ordinance of 13 December 2013
[AS 2013 5371; 2018 2279] on Electronic Voting is repealed.
This Ordinance comes into force on 1 July 2022.

mainBody.p: (Art. 2 paras 1 let. k and 2, 9, 10 paras 1 and 2 and 16 para. 1)

level.heading: Technical and administrative requirements for electronic voting
Definitions

blockList.listIntroduction: In addition to Article 2, the following expressions mean:
voting secrecy is a situation in which no person or component has the following data:

item.p: votes cast or data indicating the content of votes cast,
data allowing the persons voting to be identified (data on voters), and
data allowing the data on voters to be matched with the votes cast;
the exclusion of premature partial results is a situation in which no person or component has the votes cast or data indicating the votes cast prematurely;

the verification reference is data sent with the voting papers to enable voters to check whether their vote has been cast correctly, in accordance with Article 5 paragraph 2 in conjunction with Number 2.5 of the Annex (e.g. a list showing a code for each voting option);

an external attacker is a person or group of persons who is not familiar with how the system has been developed or how it operates, who has average resources and expertise, from whom an attack originates; their motives may include political activism and financial gain;

an internal attacker is a person or group of persons involved in the development or operation of the system from whom an attack originates; their motives may include political activism, financial gain, or the intention to harm their employer;

a hostile organisation is a group of individuals with substantial resources and above-average expertise that is the source of an attack; it may also be supported by a state; its motives may be to obtain data for profiling purposes, to disrupt a ballot or to influence the results of the ballot;
an attacker is a person, group of persons or organisation as defined in Numbers 1.4-1.6;
an electronic ballot box is storage space in which the votes cast can be stored until they are decrypted and counted;
a system log is a log established from the infrastructure components to monitor the system and investigate incidents.

level.heading: Cryptographic protocol requirements for complete verifiability (Art. 5)

item.p: System participants

blockList.listIntroduction: The cryptographic protocol regulates the tasks of the following abstract system participants:

item.p: voter / person voting
user device
set-up component
untrustworthy system (any component excluding the other components listed in this Number; UT system)
print component
one or more groups of control components
auditors
auditors’ technical aids
Communication channels

blockList.listIntroduction: The cryptographic protocol may provide the following communication channels to enable system participants to exchange messages:

item.p: voter / person voting ↔ user device
user device ↔ UT system
set-up component ↔ UT system
control component ↔ UT system
UT system → print component
UT system → auditors’ technical aid
print component → voter / person voting
set-up component → auditors’ technical aid
auditors ↔ auditors’ technical aid
bi-directional channels for communication between control components
Attackers

The cryptographic protocol must provide protection against an attacker attempting to tamper with the votes and the result, to breach voting secrecy or to obtain premature partial results (Nos 2.5–2.8).

blockList.listIntroduction: The assumption must be made that an attacker has the following abilities:

item.p: He can take control of all untrustworthy system participants (cf. No 2.4), so that they share all the secret data with him and act without restriction according to his instructions.
He can read or prevent delivery of all messages that are exchanged on untrustworthy channels and feed in his own messages as he pleases.
Trustworthy and untrustworthy system participants and communication channels

System participants and communication channels are considered either to be «trustworthy» or «untrustworthy». The permitted trust assumptions for individual system participants are governed by Number 2.9.

blockList.listIntroduction: Trustworthy system participants and communication channels are regarded as protected against attackers. For the cryptographic protocol, the following assumptions may be made:

item.p: Trustworthy system participants keep private data secure and only carry out operations defined by the cryptographic protocol.
Trustworthy communication channels keep transmitted messages private and protect them from manipulation.
Requirement for the cryptographic protocol: individual verifiability

blockList.listIntroduction: The voter is given proofs in accordance with Article 5 paragraph 2 in conjunction with Article 6 letters a and b to confirm that no attacker:

item.p: has altered any partial vote before the vote has been registered as cast in conformity with the system;
has maliciously cast a vote on the voter’s behalf which has subsequently been registered as a vote cast in conformity with the system and counted.
Requirement for the cryptographic protocol: universal verifiability

blockList.listIntroduction: The auditors receive a proof in accordance with Article 5 paragraph 3 letter a in conjunction with Article 6 letters a and c to confirm that no attacker:

item.p: after the votes were registered as cast in conformity with the system, has altered or misappropriated any partial votes before the result was determined;
has inserted any votes or partial votes not cast in conformity with the system which were taken into account in determining the result.
Requirements for the cryptographic protocol: preserving voting secrecy and excluding premature partial results
It must be ensured that no attacker is able to breach voting secrecy or establish premature partial results unless he can control the voters or their user devices.
There is no obligation to prevent attacks that limit the number of tallied votes to the degree that all partial votes for a question, list or candidate are the same.

It must be ensured that no attacker can take control of user devices unnoticed by manipulating the user device software on the server. The person voting must be able to verify that the server has provided his or her user device with the correct software with the correct parameters, in particular the public key for encrypting the vote.
Requirement for the cryptographic protocol: effective authentication

content.p: It must be ensured that no attacker can cast a vote in conformity with the system without having control over the voters concerned.

item.p: List of trustworthy and untrustworthy system participants
For soundness of the proofs referred to in Number 2.5

blockList.listIntroduction: The following system participants are considered untrustworthy:

item.p: user device
UT system
three out of four control components per group, leaving open which three they are
a significant proportion of voters
auditors
auditors’ technical aids

blockList.listIntroduction: The following system participants may be considered trustworthy:

item.p: set-up component
print component
one of four control components per group, leaving open which one it is
For soundness of the proofs referred to in Number 2.6

blockList.listIntroduction: The following system participants are regarded as untrustworthy:

item.p: user device
UT system
three of four control components per group, leaving open which three they are
a significant proportion of voters
set-up component
print component

blockList.listIntroduction: The following system participants may be considered trustworthy:

item.p: one of four control components per group, leaving open which one it is
one auditor in any group, leaving open which auditor it is
one technical aid from a trustworthy auditor, leaving open which aid it is
For preserving voting secrecy and excluding premature partial results in accordance with Number 2.7

blockList.listIntroduction: The following system participants are regarded as untrustworthy:

item.p: UT system
three of four control components per group, leaving open which three they are
a significant proportion of voters
auditors
auditors’ technical aids

blockList.listIntroduction: The following system participants may be considered trustworthy:

item.p: set-up component
print component
user device
one of four control components per group, leaving open which one it is
If an entire group of control components is used by a private system operator, none of these control components is considered trustworthy.
For the effectiveness of the authentication referred to in Number 2.8

blockList.listIntroduction: The following system participants are regarded as untrustworthy:

item.p: UT system
three of four control components per group, leaving open which three they are
a significant proportion of voters
auditors
auditors’ technical aids
user device

blockList.listIntroduction: The following system participants may be considered trustworthy:

item.p: set-up component
print component
one of four control components per group, leaving open which one it is
List of trustworthy and untrustworthy communication channels

blockList.listIntroduction: The following communication channels are considered untrustworthy:

item.p: user device ↔ UT system
set-up component ↔ UT system
control component ↔ UT system
UT system → print component
UT system → auditors’ technical aids
bi-directional channels for communication between control components

blockList.listIntroduction: The following communication channels may be considered trustworthy:

item.p: voter / person voting ↔ user device
auditors’ technical aid ↔ auditors
set-up component → auditors’ technical aids
print component → voter / person voting
Additional requirements for the soundness of the proofs
The probability of an attacker being able to falsify a proof under Number 2.5 if he changes a partial vote, suppresses a partial vote or casts a vote in someone else’s name must not exceed 0.1%.

The probability of an attacker being able to falsify a proof under Number 2.6 if he causes the calculated result to deviate by 0.1% from the correct result by altering and suppressing votes cast in conformity with the system or by entering votes not cast in conformity with the system may not exceed 1% per proposal, list or candidate selection.

If the probability of an attacker being able to falsify a proof under Number 2.6 is not negligible in the cryptographic sense
This corresponds for example to the probability of being able, without knowing the key, to decrypt an encrypted value that has been encrypted with a secure algorithm and corresponding parameterisation. , it must be possible to reduce the probability of success as desired by repeated tallying, by providing the auditors with an additional, independent proof under Number 2.6 for each count.
Functional requirements for the voting process with implications for the cryptographic protocol
Only one vote can be cast with the authentication credentials assigned to a voter.
The person voting enters their vote on the user device.
The person voting can change the vote up to the point of confirming the decision to cast it and can check the vote against a summary.
After the person voting has had the opportunity to check the vote against the summary, he or she confirms on the user device that he or she wants to cast the vote as entered.

The proofs of correct voting under Number 2.5 must be divided into at least two sequential items of proof. Any indication presented as an item of proof must make a genuine contribution to the soundness of the proof referred to in Number 2.5.
The user device displays the first item of proof to the person voting after he or she has confirmed on the user device that he or she wants to cast the vote.
The user device will not display the next item of proof to the voting person until the voting person has entered into the user device that the previous item of proof is correct.
By confirming that the penultimate item of proof is correct, the voting person confirms his or her decision to cast the vote definitively.
The group of control components registers the vote as having been cast in conformity with the system when it has received confirmation of the definitive decision to cast the vote.

When the person voting has checked the last item of proof as being correct, the voting process is complete. The last item of proof should be made particularly easy to check, by limiting the check as far as possible to the correct display of a single code or other simple indication.
If voting data are imported, a setup component or a print component must no longer be considered trustworthy from that point on.
Requirements for the definition and description of the cryptographic protocol

Wherever possible, building-blocks are used that are in widespread use worldwide and have been thoroughly scrutinised by experts. Standards, reference projects and academic publications can be used as a benchmark. Derogations and cases of doubt must be dealt with separately in the context of the risk assessment referred to in Article 4.

Instructions must not be underspecified. Individual instructions must restrict the options for implementation to such a degree that any form of implementation that the instructions allow is also compliant with meeting the cryptographic protocol requirements.
It may be assumed that trustworthy channels exist to distribute electronic certificates among system participants. Number 3.8 applies.
Proofs of compliance with the cryptographic protocol requirements
A symbolic and a cryptographic proof of compliance must demonstrate that the cryptographic protocol meets the requirements in Numbers 2.1–2.12.
The proofs of compliance must directly refer to the protocol description that forms the basis for system development.

The proofs of compliance relating to basic cryptographic components may be provided according to generally accepted security assumptions and constructions (e.g. «random oracle model», «decisional Diffie-Hellman assumption», «Fiat-Shamir heuristic»).

level.heading: Requirements for trustworthy components in accordance with Number 2 and for their operation

item.p: The operation of the set-up component and at least one control component in the group which contains part of the key for decrypting the votes is the direct responsibility of the canton and must take place within its infrastructure. Outsourcing to a private system operator is not permitted.
Sufficient entropy must be ensured when selecting random values, in particular for set-up components and control components.
Auditors must verify the proofs referred to in Number 2.6 at least once and must use a technical aid referred to in Number 2 for this purpose.

The operational requirements for set-up components in accordance with Number 3 also apply to technical aids used by the auditors. Within the scope of their responsibility under cantonal law, the auditors may provide for derogations.

With the exception of the components mentioned under Numbers 3.1 and 3.3, the canton may delegate the operation of any part of the system, including the control components and the print component, to private service providers. A private operator of the print component may only perform operational tasks that are required for preparation, packaging and delivery.
Trustworthy components (set-up components, print components, auditors’ technical aids and control components) must be set up, updated, configured and secured in an observable process.
Before installing software, all programs must be checked using an official and trustworthy reference to ensure that the files are the correct and unaltered version.

When other system participants’ electronic certificates are installed, their authenticity must be ensured. To that end, there should be a manual process in which people transfer the electronic certificates from one machine to another via a physical data carrier in accordance with 3.13.
The timing for updating all software of trustworthy components must be such that the expected benefits outweigh the potential hazards.

Set-up components, print components and auditors’ technical aids that are involved in any way in the processing of critical data must be physically monitored during the entire computing time by two persons and until any critical data have been deleted or securely stored. At most, they may be interconnected by visible physical cables so that it is as evident as possible that no other machines can access them until the confidential data is destroyed.
Trustworthy components may not be connected to the internet when installing or updating software.
In principle, critical data must be destroyed after use. If there are good reasons, secure storage of the data carrier is also permitted as an alternative.

Data exchange or storage media, such as USB flash drives, must be removed after the data has been uploaded to the trustworthy components and may only be reused before the data is destroyed if there was no critical data on the trustworthy component before the data was uploaded.

Data exchange or storage media must be reformatted and any data on them must be destroyed before they are used with the aid of a component operated in accordance with the requirements for trustworthy components.

Logical or physical access to trustworthy components or data carriers containing critical data must be impossible without another person becoming aware of it, for example by having to assist in granting access (strict two person principle).

blockList.listIntroduction: Success in gaining unauthorised access to a control component should not as far as possible give any advantage in an attempt to access another control component unnoticed. In addition to the requirements set out in Number 3, the following requirements apply in this respect:

item.p: If a person has physical or logical access to a control component, that person may not have access to any other control component.
The hardware, the operating systems and the monitoring systems for the control components should be as distinct as possible from each other.
The control components should be connected to different local networks.
A control component must take the form of a physical device. Virtualisation across multiple physical devices is not permitted.

Control components must be designed to recognise unpermitted instances of access and to alert the persons responsible. The persons responsible should arrange external monitoring measures, such as the monitoring and the manipulation-resistant logging of network traffic or physical monitoring with cameras that are under their control. The persons responsible must be considered to be particularly trustworthy and reliable.
Trustworthy components may perform only the intended operations.

The software for the auditors’ technical aids must be obtained from a different system developer from the one who developed the main part of the software for the other system components. The publication of the software for the technical aid under a licence that meets the criteria for open source software
See the definition in the Practice Guide to Open Source Software in the Federal Administration, version 1.0 of 19.12.2019, ch. 1; available from: Swiss Federal Chancellery, CH-3003 Bern; www.bk.admin.ch > Digitale Transformation und IKT Lenkung > Bundesarchitektur > Open Source Software (OSS) (available in German only). may justify an exception. If auditors use several technical aids, this provision applies to at least one of the technical aids.
All procedures for dealing with trustworthy components must be documented in writing and in a manner that is easily understood by the persons concerned.
Any access to and use of a trusted component or data carrier containing critical data must be logged.

level.heading: Voting process

item.p: The person voting must declare that he or she is aware of the rules on electronic voting and of his or her own responsibilities.

Before casting a vote, the person voting is notified that he or she is taking part in a ballot in the same way as voting by post or voting in person at the ballot box. The person voting may only cast his or her vote after confirming that he or she has taken note of this.
When voting, the person voting is requested to check the proofs in accordance with Number 2.5 against the verification reference and to report any doubts as to its correctness to the canton.
At any time before casting an electronic vote definitively, the voter may still choose to cast his or her vote via a conventional voting channel.
The client-side system as it appears to the person voting does not influence the person voting in his or her decision on how to vote.
The user guidance must not lead persons voting to cast hasty or ill-considered votes.
The system does not offer the person voting any functionality allowing them to print out or store their vote.
The person voting is not shown any information after the voting process is completed about the content of the vote that has been encrypted and cast.

A voter who is unable to cast a vote because third parties have cast a vote using his or her voting papers unlawfully may still be allowed by the canton to vote provided the canton declares the unlawfully cast vote null and void. Voting secrecy in accordance with Number 2.7 must be preserved.
Voters with disabilities may be provided with a simplified procedure for checking the proofs. Only in such a case are derogations from the requirements set out in Number 2.9.1 permitted.
As long as the system has not registered confirmation of a definitive electronic vote, the voter may still choose to cast his or her vote via a conventional voting channel.

The use of a means of authentication independent of electronic voting is permitted. Effects on the integrity of the verification of the right to vote and the preservation of voting secrecy must be examined in detail as part of the risk assessment.

level.heading: Preparations for the ballot

item.p: If the electoral register data is imported from a third-party system that is outside the canton’s control, the data must be encrypted and signed. The signature must be verified on receipt of the data. For delivery to the printing office, the provisions of Number 7 take precedence.
The data required to examine the proofs in accordance with Number 2.6 must be handed over to the auditors.

level.heading: Requirements for polling cards

item.p: If possible, the polling cards shall be designed so as to allow voters with a disability barrier-free access to electronic voting.
Security elements on the polling card (e.g scratch codes) may only be used if there is a confirmation that the concealed information is well protected against unauthorised reading.
If it is decided not to use security elements to protect confidential information on the voting card, organisational procedures must be in place to ensure security.

level.heading: Requirements for printing offices

item.p: The printing data used to produce the polling cards are transmitted encrypted and signed. Alternatively, a data carrier containing this data may be delivered in person. In this case, the data carrier must be transported and delivered to the printing office by two persons, who must both stay with the data carrier until it is delivered.

The encryption must meet the requirements of eCH standard 0014
eCH-0014: Standards and Architectures for eGovernment Applications Switzerland (SAGA.ch), version 9.0 of 09.12.2019; the standard can be obtained from and viewed free of charge from the eCH Association, Mainaustrasse 30, P.O. Box, 8034 Zurich, www.ech.ch , Chapter 7.5. If encryption is symmetric, the secret decryption key is sent to the persons responsible at the printing office via a secure secondary channel.
The person responsible at the printing office who receives the data carrier must sign an acknowledgement of receipt.

For the data carrier containing the print data, the component on which the critical data is decrypted and all components that process the critical data, the provisions for the print component as set out in Number 3 apply.
The persons responsible at the printing office carry out a material quantity check.
After printing the polling cards, the printing office must destroy the data received.
If the printing office also carries out the packaging and dispatch of the polling cards, these must be packaged together with the voting papers immediately after printing.

The channel between the printing office and the voters may only be considered trustworthy if the bodies responsible under cantonal law deliver the packaged voting papers to the voters by post or ensure that it is handed over in person.

level.heading: Information and instructions

item.p: The body responsible at cantonal level must issue guidelines on providing information to citizens about electronic voting.
The guidelines ensure that the information is authorised by the responsible bodies.
Tips and instructions on vote casting are given on the internet along with information on voters’ responsibilities. This should counter over-hasty or ill-considered vote casting behaviour.
Verifiability, further security measures and the procedure in the event of anomalies are explained to voters in an accessible manner.
Voters are told what they have to pay attention to in order to cast their vote securely.
Voters are given instructions on how to delete their vote from all the memories on the device used for entering the vote.
Voters may request support if they have questions about electronic voting.

Voters are requested to report incorrectly displayed proofs in accordance with Number 2.5 such as verification codes or other verification steps with negative results to the body responsible at cantonal level. This request is also made in the instructions sent out with the voting papers.
Voters are requested to keep the voting papers with the security elements in fulfilment of Number 2.5 securely until they cast their final vote or until the voting process is concluded.

Voters are given the information required to check the authenticity of the website and the server used for voting. The informative value of a successful check must be supported by the use of cryptographic resources according to the best practices.

The information essential for secure voting is sent with the voting papers. Voters are told that if in doubt, they should comply with the information in the voting papers rather than the information displayed on the user device.
The measures taken to preserve voting secrecy are explained to voters.
Known flaws and the need for action associated with them are communicated transparently.

The auditors should be suitably informed about and trained in the processes that determine the accuracy of the result, the preservation of voting secrecy and the exclusion of premature partial results (for example key generation, printing the voting papers, decryption and tallying). They must be able to understand the essential aspects of the processes and their significance.

level.heading: Opening and closing the electronic voting channel

content.p: The electronic voting channel is only available during the permitted period.

level.heading: Conformity check and storing finalised votes

content.p: Votes not cast in conformity with the system are not stored in the electronic ballot box.

level.heading: Tallying votes in the electronic ballot box

item.p: The decryption of the votes and the tallying may not begin before Polling Sunday.
The canton carries out the decryption and tallying within its own infrastructure.
The canton must ensure that the decryption of votes and their tallying is documented. The minutes are released by the body responsible at cantonal level.

From the decryption of votes to the transmission of the result of the ballot, any access to the system or to any of its components must be made jointly by at least two persons; it must be recorded in writing and it must be possible for the auditors to check it.
If the result data is transmitted to a third-party system that is outside the canton’s control, the data must be encrypted and signed.
The system allows the polling card to be used to determine whether someone has cast an electronic vote.
Auditors must be present during decryption and tallying. The cantons may permit additional remote auditing work.
If components used to tally votes are not trustworthy in accordance with Number 2.4, the same requirements apply to these components as to set-up components under Number 3.
The auditors exercise their responsibility in accordance with cantonal law when examining the proofs in accordance with Number 2.6.

The body responsible at cantonal level submits all relevant indicators of the correctness of the result to the auditors. This includes, in addition to the proofs in accordance with Number 2.6, in particular the number and nature of anomalies reported to the canton by voters.

The canton anticipates any anomalies and, in consultation with the bodies concerned, draws up an emergency plan specifying the appropriate course of action. It creates transparency towards the public.
Statistical methods must be used to check the plausibility of the result, provided they are available and there is sufficient data.

level.heading: Confidential data

item.p: It is guaranteed that neither employees nor externals hold data that allow a connection to be made between the identity of persons voting and the votes they have cast.
It is guaranteed that neither employees nor externals hold data before the decryption of the votes that allow the premature determination of partial results.
The canton may not pass on to private companies its part of the key for decrypting the votes which it has on the control component that it operates in accordance with Number 3.1.
The canton must treat the results of the ballot as confidential between the time the votes are decrypted and the time of publication.
The canton must ensure that data that indicate whether a voter has voted electronically are treated as confidential.
The canton must treat the individual votes as confidential after they have been tallied.
The canton must ensure that vote and election results in small constituencies are treated as confidential.

Following validation and in accordance with a predetermined and documented process, all data created as part of the electronic ballot that relate to the individual votes received and that are classified as confidential must be destroyed.

level.heading: Threats

item.p: The threats listed in Numbers 13.3-13.40 are of a general nature and form a basis; this must be added to. They relate to the security objectives and must be taken into account when identifying risks. Depending on the system vulnerabilities identified, when the various bodies carry out their risk assessments, the list should be updated with full details based on the actual circumstances and depending on the specific threat.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following are considered to be potential threats:

item.p: inadvertent or intended electronic or physical threats from internal or external actors;
threats resulting from a malfunction of the system or system-supporting elements.
